name: Josh Shapiro
role: Governor of Pennsylvania (2023-present); Pennsylvania attorney general (2017-2023)
summary: Shapiro is a Democratic governor whose record combines labor-friendly and socially liberal commitments (a $15 minimum wage, opposition to right-to-work, abortion access, LGBTQ civil rights, ending the death penalty) with business tax cuts, faster permitting, support for school-choice scholarships and an all-of-the-above energy approach. He supports Israel as a Jewish state and a two-state solution while criticizing Netanyahu's government.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Proposed raising Pennsylvania's minimum wage from $7.25 to $15 in 2023 and again in the 2025-26 budget address.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Told the All-In hosts a wealth tax is not on his agenda and boasted of tax cuts, while also saying people at the top should pay their fair share; he has proposed no significant increases on high earners.

unions-good.rationale: Said all workers should have the right to organize and bargain collectively, pledged Pennsylvania will never be a right-to-work state and expanded project labor agreements.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Proposed private-equity safeguards in health care, pharmacy benefit manager reform, utility billing transparency and strict standards for data center developers, and as attorney general charged Energy Transfer over pipeline construction. He has also cut business taxes and licensing delays, so the answer is moderate.

cut-welfare.rationale: Proposed raising the minimum monthly SNAP benefit by 50 percent in his 2023 budget and in 2026 attacked federal cuts to SNAP and Medicaid; he does not describe welfare as creating dependency.

strong-leader.rationale: He opposes concentrated executive power, yet explicitly used executive action on data centers when the Senate would not act.

state-harmful.rationale: His record as attorney general and governor is of using and expanding state programs (health, schools, housing, public safety) and arguing government should deliver results.

limit-guns.rationale: In the 2024 budget address asked why the state tolerates background-check loopholes that let criminals get guns and urged lawmakers to close them; as attorney general backed the federal ghost-gun rule. These are targeted restrictions, not strict limits on ownership, so the answer is mild.

empower-police-military.rationale: Funded additional State Police cadet classes, a dedicated police funding source and recruitment incentives; no stated position on more authority or on the military.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: As Montgomery County commissioner chair in 2013 helped issue marriage licences to same-sex couples in defiance of state law; his campaign describes him as a strong supporter of LGBT civil rights.

abortion-legal.rationale: Pledged that abortion access will remain protected while he is governor ('women will always have the right to choose'), warned against going back to pre-Roe law and ended state funding for an anti-abortion counselling contract.

limit-growth.rationale: Describes his approach as pro-growth, touts record job gains and investment, and frames environmental protection as compatible with growth rather than a limit on it.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Proposed raising the 2030 clean-electricity target to 30% and net-zero by 2050, but was non-committal on RGGI and later signed withdrawal from it; not framed as drastic action.

expand-nuclear.rationale: His campaign plan funded research and design of zero-carbon technology including nuclear; later energy plans included small modular reactors. No direct call to expand existing nuclear capacity.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Has criticized the Trump administration's broad tariffs as raising costs for consumers, farmers and small businesses; he has not stated a general view on protecting domestic industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: His personally promoted budget funds startup capital, clinical trials and the innovation network.

one-party-rule.rationale: He explicitly rejects one party solving the Commonwealth’s problems alone and defends multiparty legislative negotiation.

democracy-best.rationale: Said 'our democracy is not a given' and that Pennsylvanians cherish it; defended free and fair elections. Has not addressed the 'even when voters choose badly' clause.

political-violence-never.rationale: Said political violence 'has no place in our society, regardless of what motivates it' after the Butler shooting and the arson attack on his residence, and repeated in September 2025 that violence of any kind has no place and the answer to speech one disagrees with is more speech.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Frames his governing around getting things done and says he does not change positions because of polling; no explicit statement on ideology.

positive-liberty.rationale: He defines real freedom through adequate public schooling, safety and pathways to employment.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Supports Israel as a Jewish state and has repeatedly said he backs a two-state solution; calls Israel a key US ally.

school-vouchers.rationale: Supported Lifeline Scholarships (vouchers for students in low-performing districts) in 2022-23, on condition that no money is taken from public schools, dropped the push in 2023 when House Democrats refused, and in the 2024 budget address again urged scholarships for poor families in struggling districts as unfinished business. Programme was targeted, not open to any school.

work-for-welfare.rationale: In his 2026 budget he rejected adding arbitrary and cumbersome requirements that push people off Medicaid, preferring higher wages, and in the 2026 debate he opposed the federal law adding Medicaid work requirements; he frames his own approach as pro-work rather than conditioning aid.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Calls for 'responsible fracking' and backs the Lightning Plan to increase energy production; also set clean-electricity goals, so the position on expanding oil, gas and coal is qualified.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He calls for accountability over federal agents’ killings of Good and Pretti and challenges unconstitutional enforcement.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Pushed equal-rights protections for LGBTQ people and defended equal voting and civil rights in office; no single direct statement of this principle.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He describes political authority as a covenant grounded in the public’s voice and vote.

separated-powers.rationale: He insists Congress must exercise its constitutional checking role rather than become a presidential rubber stamp.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: He explicitly says diversity makes society stronger while opposing antisemitism and anti-Muslim bigotry.

party-controls-media.rationale: He condemns the federal government’s censorship of political expression rather than government control of public debate.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: He rejects politicians deciding which books children may read as an infringement of family freedom.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Criticized the Trump administration for alienating allies and signaling that Europe is on its own, saying strong leaders stand with their allies; he did not address military bases or NATO by name.

death-penalty.rationale: Said he will issue no execution warrants, will grant reprieves, and asked the legislature to abolish capital punishment: 'The Commonwealth shouldn't be in the business of putting people to death. Period.' He had earlier supported it for the worst crimes; the 2023 position is recent and clear.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Backs a two-state solution, which implies territorial compromise, while calling Netanyahu's course dangerous; he has not discussed historic-homeland claims directly.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He insists officeholders owe allegiance to the Constitution rather than personal obedience to the president.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Pledged to pass housing, schooling and employment nondiscrimination protections for LGBTQ people, which restrict private discrimination.

elective-rulers.rationale: He explicitly defends free, fair elections and the peaceful transfer of political authority.

corporate-influence.rationale: Told Senate Republicans to stop cowering to special interests such as insurance companies and Catholic Church lobbyists on the child abuse civil window; a single remark, not a general claim about corporate lobbying.

public-access-to-information.rationale: As a state representative he co-chaired the 2007 legislative reform commission, which pushed to strengthen public records access and helped form the basis of the Right-to-Know Law; the position is the commission's, with Shapiro as co-chair, and he has not restated it as a general right since.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: His record is of backing LGBT civil rights, marriage licences for same-sex couples and nondiscrimination law; no statement on criminal law specifically.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He explicitly rejects political censorship; his off-duty employee conduct rule complicates that commitment, with its application to dissent disputed and his office affirming constitutional rights.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Pledged nondiscrimination protections for LGBTQ people, filed an attorney general brief supporting a transgender student's bathroom access, and opposed banning transgender girls from girls' teams. Has not addressed legal gender recognition itself.

islam-incompatible.rationale: He rejects claims that Muslims do not belong in American society and calls for unity against Islamophobia.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Record of funding and recruiting police and corrections officers (cadet classes, hiring bonuses); no proposals to replace police or prisons.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Backed workers' right to bargain collectively and opposed right-to-work, which implies collectively negotiated terms; he has not addressed the individual-contract alternative directly.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: He personally advanced the enacted Working Pennsylvanians Tax Credit, tied to federal earned-income eligibility.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Stated Pennsylvania will never be a right-to-work state and pledged to veto right-to-work legislation, which is the policy this statement describes.

voter-id.rationale: At the October 2026 debate said he is open to putting a voter ID bill on his desk, provided it is not built on conspiracy theories and does not disenfranchise voters; he has not endorsed a proof-of-citizenship requirement.

women-suffrage.rationale: He presents women gaining equal voting rights as necessary democratic progress.

notes:
Death penalty: he supported it for the worst crimes (including the 2018 Pittsburgh synagogue shooter) before announcing in February 2023 that he would sign no warrants and wants abolition; the 2023 position is used. Vouchers: backed Lifeline Scholarships in 2022-23 but dropped the push in 2023. Many themes are null because the sources opened (budget and inaugural addresses, campaign-era issue coverage, press reporting) do not state positions on them; no answers were inferred from party. Wikipedia attributes a 'worst leaders of all time' remark about Netanyahu to him that could not be confirmed; it was not used.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass; existing audit read only for metadata, notes and sources. Full budget speeches, inaugural address and two 2026 long interviews downloaded and searched across all themes. All 490 statements and remaining nulls reviewed, including all ten priority statements. No inference from Democratic membership or Judaism. Criticism of communist China does not establish a general policy of defeating communism; apprenticeship coordination does not establish a theory rejecting class struggle. Cannabis reform is not legalization of all drugs. Healthcare subsidies do not establish a universal government healthcare program. His assisted-dying answer expressly remains unsettled and is null; the host’s views are not his. Latest constitutional defenses are weighed alongside his August executive order: the order invokes existing agency powers rather than declaring the executive above law. His current data-center restrictions supersede unqualified readings of earlier investment promotion. Capital punishment reversal is explicit and reaffirmed in 2026. The former-staffer harassment settlement and clergy-abuse report were checked as context; no personal NDA policy inferred merely from an office settlement or a grand jury recommendation. No position on universal press-access law inferred from his fight to publish one report. Sources did not substantiate precise ancient or revolutionary constitutional/economic theories, general AI replacement of government, or the listed globalism propositions. His May 2024 on/off-duty employee conduct amendment and the contemporaneous administration response were also reviewed. The code’s contested scope qualifies the opposition-repression answer; it is not treated as a general public hate-speech ban or proof that independent organizations were prohibited. The administration says it protects lawful First Amendment exercise.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent third pass (budget addresses 2023-2026, 2026 debate recaps, energy, data-center, tariff, Iran and Ukraine statements). He is running for re-election on 3 Nov 2026 and has not declared a presidential candidacy. Death penalty: supported it for heinous crimes before 2022; the 2023 reversal and no-warrant policy is used and was repeated at the October 2026 debate. Vouchers: supported Lifeline Scholarships in 2023, vetoed the provision, and says he is still open; recorded low. Energy: he left RGGI in the November 2025 budget deal after proposing PACER; recorded as mixed on drastic climate action.
